name: Bappanadu Dolu Utsava
description: Renowned coastal festival founded on the historical friendship of Goddess Durga and Muslim merchant Bappa Byari, celebrated with non-stop beating of giant copper Dolu drums.
keyPractices: Distribution of first Prasada to Bappa Byari descendants
culturalSignificance: A living beacon of coastal inter-faith brotherhood and community cohesion.
relatedStories: ST-007: Legend of Bappanadu and Bappa Byari
source: Bappanadu Temple Endowment Epigraphs, South Canara District Manual

name: Kateel Mesha Jathre & Agni Keli
description: The monumental annual car festival of Goddess Durgaparameshwari on the Nandini river island, culminating in the fiery Agni Keli torch-hurling ritual.
culturalSignificance: Ritually reenacts the annihilation of demon Arunasura by Goddess Durga manifesting as a swarm of bees (Bhramari).
relatedStories: ST-004: Myth of Kateel and Demon Arunasura

name: Padubidri Dakkebali Utsava
description: Nocturnal Tantric festival dedicated to Naga spirits and Mother Goddess Mahalingeshwari, famous for the hypnotic Dakke percussion and spiraling trance dances.
keyPractices: Ecstatic Patri trance dances holding areca flowers
culturalSignificance: Vital living link between coastal evergreen grove preservation and esoteric Tantric serpent worship.
relatedStories: ST-001: Origin of Tulunadu Serpent Groves
source: Peter J. Claus, Padubidri Temple Records
verificationStatus: Verified from primary coastal ethnographic documentation

name: Siri Jatre
description: Mass assembly where thousands of women congregate under the full moon at sacred Alade groves, entering spontaneous therapeutic possession under the guidance of Kumara bards.
keyPractices: Mass trance possession of women holds areca flowers
culturalSignificance: The world’s largest documented living feminist oral tradition and folk psychotherapy ritual.
relatedStories: ST-003: Epic of Princess Siri and Aliyasantana Justice
source: Lauri Honko (The Siri Epic, 2 vols), Finnish Academy of Science and Letters

name: Udupi Paryaya Mahotsava
description: The monumental ascension ceremony where the pontiff of one of the eight sovereign Ashta Mathas assumes worship and feeding rights of Sri Krishna Matha for two years.
keyPractices: Ceremonial handover of Akshaya Patra and keys
culturalSignificance: A 500-year-old operational model of rotating decentralized democratic monastic governance.
relatedStories: ST-005: Sri Madhvacharya and Kanakadasa at Kanakana Kindi

name: Laksha Deepotsava (Dharmasthala)
description: Lighting of over 100,000 earthen oil lamps across the Netravati valley accompanied by all-faith assemblies and grand chariot processions.
culturalSignificance: Reinforces the four pillars of Dharmasthala: Anna (food), Abhaya (refuge), Aushadha (medicine), and Vidya (education).
relatedStories: ST-008: Legend of Barmana Heggade and the Four Dharma Daivas

name: Gokarna Mahashivaratri & Brahma Rathotsava
description: Epic car festival where two massive wooden chariots (Maha Ratha and Chikka Ratha) are hauled through the temple streets to honor the Atmalinga.
keyPractices: Pulling of giant wooden temple chariots
Holy dip at Koti Theertha and Arabian Sea
All-night Vedic chanting and Bilva archana
culturalSignificance: The preeminent Shaivite coastal congregation honoring the foundational Atmalinga of Ravana legend.
relatedRituals: RIT-023: Atmalinga Abhisheka & Koti Theertha Snana
relatedStories: ST-006: Ravana, Ganesha, and the Rooting of the Atmalinga
source: Gokarna Mahatmya (Skanda Purana), Uttara Kannada District Gazetteer

name: Polali Chendu Utsava
description: Unique 5-day football tournament played with a handmade leather ball on the temple fields between territorial divisions Malgodu and Thodu.
keyPractices: Consecration of the leather ball by temple elders
culturalSignificance: Transformation of ancient village clan battles into consecrated athletic worship of Goddess Rajarajeshwari.
relatedStories: ST-009: King Suratha and the 8th-Century Lepa Murti of Polali

name: Keddasa Earth Fertility Observance
description: Universal three-day holiday for the soil, observing the menstruation of Mother Earth by prohibiting all digging, plowing, and cutting of vegetation.
keyPractices: Bathing the earth on third day with oil and turmeric
Preparation of Keddaseda Kudu medicinal horsegram porridge
culturalSignificance: Indigenous ecological conservation covenant enforcing restorative rest for topsoil.
relatedStories: ST-001: Sacred Earth Covenants of Tulunadu
source: Peter J. Claus, Indira Ballal research

name: Aati Amavasya (Kashaya & Ancestral Day)
description: Pre-dawn medicinal festival where every family harvests and drinks the bitter immune-boosting potion from the bark of the sacred Paale tree.
keyPractices: Pre-dawn stripping of Paale bark with stones
Sea bath at Someshwara and mountain dip at Narahari Parvatha
culturalSignificance: Synchronizes indigenous human biology with monsoon seasonal pathogens through traditional pharmacology.
relatedCommunities: Universal coastal population (Tuluvas, Konkanis, Bearys, Brahmins)
relatedStories: ST-010: The Medicinal Covenant of the Paale Tree
epistemicStatus: Documented living practice & Botanical traditional account

name: Udupi Krishna Janmashtami & Mosaru Kudike
description: Vibrant celebration featuring midnight Arghya to Lord Krishna followed on the next day by Mosaru Kudike (breaking earthen curd pots suspended on tall poles).
keyPractices: Clay idol immersion in Madhwa Sarovara
culturalSignificance: Transforms the scholastic monasticism of Udupi into a joyous democratic street festival of music and dance.
relatedCommunities: Youth guilds from all coastal communities
source: Udupi Matha Chronicles, Karnataka State Gazetteers

name: Nagara Panchami
description: Premier monsoon festival honoring serpent deities where families pour cold cow milk and tender coconut water over stone Naga idols in sacred Nagabanas.
keyPractices: Milk abhisheka to stone Naga idols
Offering of Pingara areca blossoms and turmeric paste
Deep reverence for biological and spiritual serpents
culturalSignificance: Guarantees the strict protection of fragile coastal evergreen sacred groves (Nagabanas) against deforestation.
relatedStories: ST-001: Parashurama and the Serpent Kings of the Western Sea
source: B.A. Saletore, Regional Temple Trust manuals
